title: Lock screen does not blur background image if it is activated twice in a row
line: Locking the screen twice in quick succession no longer leaves the lock screen wallpaper unblurred.
explanation: A second lock request while the greeter is starting makes KSldApp send it SIGUSR1 to switch to immediate lock. If that arrives before the greeter's main() has blocked the signal and installed its handler, the default action kills the greeter; KSldApp treats that as a crash and restarts it with QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software, where the blur (and the round avatar mask) are not rendered. KSldApp now starts the greeter with SIGUSR1 already blocked, so the signal stays pending until the greeter unblocks it after installing its handler.

commits.message:
ksldapp: don't let an early SIGUSR1 kill a starting greeter

Locking twice in a row sent SIGUSR1 to a greeter that had not set up its
handler yet, which killed it and restarted it with software rendering,
so the lock screen lost its blur. Start it with SIGUSR1 blocked instead.

BUG: 475142

media.caption: Two back-to-back Lock calls on master: greeter crashed and restarted in software rendering, wallpaper sharp
Same two Lock calls with the fix: no greeter restart, wallpaper blurred

review.text: Excellent root-cause diagnosis and minimal fix for a longstanding race: locking twice in rapid succession sent SIGUSR1 before kscreenlocker_greet installed its handler, killing the greeter and causing KSldApp to restart it with QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software (which broke both wallpaper blur and circular avatar masking). Blocking SIGUSR1 in QProcess::setChildProcessModifier uses async-signal-safe POSIX calls and preserves the pending signal across execve() until the greeter installs its handler and unblocks it. Verified cleanly with screenshots, journal/SigBlk checks, and passing autotests.

reviews.text: Excellent root-cause diagnosis and minimal fix for a longstanding race: locking twice in rapid succession sent SIGUSR1 before kscreenlocker_greet installed its handler, killing the greeter and causing KSldApp to restart it with QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software (which broke both wallpaper blur and circular avatar masking). Blocking SIGUSR1 in QProcess::setChildProcessModifier uses async-signal-safe POSIX calls and preserves the pending signal across execve() until the greeter installs its handler and unblocks it. Verified cleanly with screenshots, journal/SigBlk checks, and passing autotests.

The root cause is real and fully explains the report: a second lock makes KSldApp SIGUSR1 the greeter, and if that lands before greeter/main.cpp blocks SIGUSR1 and registers KSignalHandler, the default action kills it. KSldApp then restarts it on the software Qt Quick backend, which loses both the blur and the round avatar mask the reporter also noticed (c15), and the 10 ms vs 1 s timing window matches. Blocking SIGUSR1 in a QProcess child modifier closes that exec-to-handler gap. It works with the greeter's existing design, which already blocks the signal, installs its handler and then unblocks it, so the pending signal is delivered rather than lost (the verify notes the running greeter's SigBlk ends up empty). The modifier only uses async-signal-safe calls, kscreenlocker is Unix-only, and the evidence (no crash/restart, hardware backend, blurred wallpaper for double and triple locks) plus the commit text match the 7-line diff.
